subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: For the same sets A = {1,2,3} and B = {2,3,4}, what is the union of A and B?
questions.explain: The union contains every element appearing in either set.

questions.q: Which class of languages can be described by regular expressions?
questions.explain: Regular expressions describe exactly the regular languages.

questions.q: In a Karnaugh map, adjacent cells are arranged so that they differ by how many variables?
questions.explain: K-map cells use Gray-code ordering so neighbours differ in one variable, enabling grouping.

questions.q: A finite state machine with output associates output with what?
options: The end of the input only
questions.explain: An FSM with output emits symbols on transitions (Mealy) or in states (Moore).

questions.q: BNF can express which feature that simple regular expressions cannot easily handle?
questions.explain: BNF can define recursive, self-referential rules giving it more power than regex.

questions.q: A half adder produces which two outputs?
questions.explain: A half adder outputs a sum (XOR) and a carry-out (AND) but has no carry-in.

questions.q: A Turing machine consists of a finite state control plus what other essential component?
questions.explain: A Turing machine reads and writes symbols on a theoretically infinite tape.

questions.q: In a regular expression, what does the Kleene star (*) mean?
questions.explain: The * quantifier matches zero or more repetitions of the preceding element.

questions.q: What is a Karnaugh map used for?
questions.explain: A K-map groups adjacent 1s to minimise a Boolean expression.

questions.q: The Boolean distributive law gives A AND (B OR C) equal to which of the following?
questions.explain: AND distributes over OR: A AND (B OR C) = (A AND B) OR (A AND C).

questions.q: What is Backus-Naur Form (BNF) used to define?
options: The colour of a screen pixel
questions.explain: BNF is a notation for formally specifying the grammar (syntax) of languages.

questions.q: If set A = {1,2,3} and set B = {2,3,4}, what is the intersection of A and B?
questions.explain: The intersection contains only elements common to both sets: 2 and 3.

questions.q: De Morgan's law also states that NOT(A OR B) is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explain: NOT(A OR B) equals NOT A AND NOT B by De Morgan's law.

questions.q: In typical regular-expression notation, what does the alternation symbol between two expressions denote?
questions.explain: The alternation operator matches either the left or the right expression.

questions.q: A syntax (railroad) diagram is an alternative graphical representation of what?
questions.explain: Syntax diagrams visually represent the same production rules as BNF.

questions.q: In a finite state machine, a state transition is triggered by what?
questions.explain: An FSM moves between states based on the current state and an input symbol.

questions.q: There is a known equivalence between regular expressions and which machine?
questions.explain: Every regular expression has an equivalent FSM and vice versa.

questions.q: The Church-Turing thesis proposes that anything intuitively computable can be computed by what?
questions.explain: It states that the Turing machine captures the notion of effective computation.

questions.q: A D-type flip-flop is primarily used to do what?
questions.explain: A D-type flip-flop latches and stores a single bit synchronised to a clock.

questions.q: In a BNF rule, the symbol ::= means what?
questions.explain: The ::= operator separates a non-terminal from its definition in BNF.

questions.q: What feature does a full adder have that a half adder lacks?
questions.explain: A full adder accepts a carry-in, letting adders be chained for multi-bit addition.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Mealy machine from a Moore machine?
options: A Mealy machine has no states
A Mealy machine's output depends on the current state and input
A Moore machine ignores all inputs
A Moore machine has no transitions
questions.explain: Mealy outputs depend on state and input, whereas Moore outputs depend only on state.

questions.q: By Boolean algebra, the expression A OR (A AND B) simplifies to what?
questions.explain: By the absorption law, A OR (A AND B) = A.

questions.q: A D-type flip-flop changes its stored value in response to what?
options: An edge of the clock signal
questions.explain: It captures the D input on a clock edge, holding it until the next edge.

questions.q: A directed graph differs from an undirected graph in that its edges have what?
questions.explain: In a directed graph each edge has an orientation from one vertex to another.

questions.q: De Morgan's law states that NOT(A AND B) is equivalent to which expression?
questions.explain: NOT(A AND B) equals NOT A OR NOT B by De Morgan's law.

questions.q: The halting problem asks whether one can determine in general if an arbitrary program will do what?
options: Halt or run forever on a given input
questions.explain: It asks whether a program halts or loops forever for a given input, which is undecidable.

questions.q: An interrupt is best described as:
options: An instruction that doubles clock speed
A permanent halt of the processor
A signal to the processor indicating an event needs immediate attention
questions.explain: An interrupt is a signal causing the CPU to suspend its current task and service the requesting event.

questions.q: In graph theory, the degree of a vertex is defined as what?
options: The number of graphs it belongs to
The number of edges connected to it
questions.explain: A vertex's degree is the count of edges incident to it.

questions.q: Excessive swapping of pages between RAM and disk, degrading performance, is known as:
questions.explain: Thrashing occurs when the system spends more time swapping pages than executing instructions.
